endorsements.quote: Reporting TRIPOD-LLM items will help users understand and appraise the quality of LLM study methods, increase transparency around study findings, reduce overinterpretation of study findings, facilitate replication and reproducibility and aid in implementing the LLM.

We encourage editors, publishers and the industry more broadly to support adherence to TRIPOD-LLM by referring to a link within the journal’s instructions to authors, enforcing its use during the submission and peer-review process and making adherence to the recommendations an expectation.

unlisted_practices: Funders should require applications for LLM studies to include a plan to report their model according to TRIPOD-LLM recommendations.
Invest in validation infrastructure beyond large academic settings so LLM evaluation and validation can be done equitably and safely.
Report LLM version, training data cut-off dates, and whether the model was frozen or dynamic during data collection.
Report prompt engineering details, inference settings, and data used to develop prompts so LLM performance is reproducible.
Report qualifications, instructions, and interassessor agreement for human assessors of LLM outputs.
Assurance labs and internal validation standards should use TRIPOD-LLM to inform the generation, verification, certification and maintenance of model cards for clinical AI.
Evaluate LLMs as a continuous process that examines trends and heterogeneity of effects across sites and over time rather than single-point estimates claiming universal validation.

screen.reason: This paper presents the TRIPOD-LLM reporting guideline/consensus statement for studies evaluating large language models in healthcare.
